name: Oli

review.reason: The official Oli specification states 31 active degrees of freedom for Oli, matching the recorded value and claim scope.
The official Oli specification states a maximum joint torque of 150 N·m for Oli, matching the recorded value and claim scope.

actuator_torque_nm.note: Spec sheet footnote: 'The maximum torque differs among motors. The value shown represents the maximum torque of the highest-torque motor.'

timeline.detail: LimX Dynamics launched the LimX Oli full-size general-purpose humanoid robot.
Oli made its public debut at the World Robot Conference (WRC) in Beijing.

source.quote: will make its public debut this week at the World Robot Conference (WRC) in Beijing
the robotics company showcased two Oli humanoids lying down on the floor and then getting back up autonomously

review.reason: The per-host request budget was reached during the review, so the source content and claim could not be re-established.

capabilities.note: From a YouTube video released 2025-10-23, covered by Interesting Engineering (published 2025-10-28); explicit 'autonomously' from the source.

source.quote: no teleoperation and is captured in 'one continuous take'

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for Oli were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: LimX's own uncut, single-take household-chores demo (published around 2026-07-25), described by LimX and Humanoids Daily as fully autonomous long-horizon mobile manipulation ('entirely autonomously'); the source does not itemize the specific objects picked and placed.

notes: Weight, battery runtime and price were not stated on the manufacturer product page or in The Robot Report's launch article fetched during this build; a 9,500 mAh / 58.8V pack and ~2-hour runtime, and a ~55 kg weight for the Lite/EDU variants, are reported on third-party retailer/aggregator listings (e.g. RobotShop) but could not be traced to a dated manufacturer statement, so these fields are omitted rather than guessed.
Oli ships in Lite, EDU and Super editions with different specs and pricing; the values recorded here are the ones stated without a variant qualifier on the manufacturer's product/news pages.
Currently sold in Mainland China only per the manufacturer's news page, with a global version described as forthcoming.

locomotion left out (2026-09-21): searched the manufacturer's own product/press page and its main launch coverage (The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum / named outlet where applicable) for a literal quote naming the propulsion ("bipedal", "legs", "walks", "wheeled base", etc.); none of the pages fetched in this pass contained a checkable sentence naming it specifically for Oli -- most pages describe height/DOF/speed without ever stating the locomotion type in words. Left out rather than inferred from photos or category. Revisit with a source that states it directly.
